output.content:
**Amazon FY2026 Q1 AI/data-center spending**

- Amazon’s Q1 FY2026 cash capital expenditure—reported as **purchases of property and equipment—was $44.203 billion**, versus **$25.019 billion** in Q1 FY2025, an increase of **$19.184 billion (76.7% year over year)**. [[1]]
- This is the appropriate reported capex measure for the quarter; it includes broad property-and-equipment spending rather than a separately disclosed “AI data-center” line item. [[1]]
- Amazon said its higher property-and-equipment investment **primarily reflected AI investments**, while its filings show that its relevant infrastructure footprint includes data-center facilities and server/networking equipment. [[2]] [[1]]
- The Q1 outlay represented about **22.1%** of Amazon’s previously stated plan to invest approximately **$200 billion in capex during FY2026**, spanning AI alongside chips, robotics, and low-Earth-orbit satellites. [[3]]
- On a trailing-12-month basis through March 31, 2026, purchases of property and equipment, net of sale proceeds and incentives, were **$147.299 billion**, up from **$87.978 billion** a year earlier; operating cash flow was **$148.531 billion**, leaving **$1.232 billion** in free cash flow. [[1]]
- Amazon therefore does **not** disclose a clean Q1 dollar amount solely for AI data centers; the defensible disclosed answer is **$44.2 billion total quarterly property-and-equipment capex**, with management attributing the overall step-up primarily to AI. [[1]] [[2]]
